design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. A guest who leaves a monthly rental on the day she arrives asks only to "pay what I owe". The policies make that charge the last of four writes: before the notice charge may be collected the stay's ledger must carry the guest-cancellation refunds owed on the pet fee, the extra-guest fee and Roamhaven's guest service fee (three prerequisite sentences in the notice-charge rule), and the service-fee refund itself is fixed only after the pet-fee and extra-guest-fee refunds are on the ledger (two prerequisite sentences in its rule). Nothing in the persona names a refund. Every amount is a multi-factor computation over the stay's frozen breakdown, the installment ledger, the cancellation date, the stay's cancellation tier, the TX-AUSTIN tax schedule and the guest's Roamhaven Rewards tier and credit ledger. Every factor ladder divides customers who really reach its write: the notice charge applies to any guest who leaves a stay in progress owing nights the cancellation keeps (a long stay paid month by month, or a stay checked in while the collection of installment 1 was still declined, on any tier), so its notice-length, later-night, fee-rate and exemption tiers are all occupied. Difficulty comes from reading the rules and the records and from arithmetic, never from choosing among tools: each policy names its own tool.

SCOPE. Task 0 is the first task; nothing was occupied. Claimed: stay_ext_departure_pet_fee_refund (refund_pet_fee_41a7068c), stay_ext_departure_extra_guest_fee_refund (refund_extra_guest_fee_b492f389), stay_ext_departure_service_fee_refund (refund_service_fee_f4bed6e4), stay_ext_departure_notice_charge (pay_notice_charge_caff8891, owner=user). Left for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisite problems, factors [6,4,4]): the travel-issue family on a check-in date (nightly travel refund, travel service-fee refund, installment 1 paid by the guest) — disjoint policies, tools and events.

DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5, 6]} -> notice charge 6, pet-fee refund 5, extra-guest-fee refund 5, service-fee refund 4.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: stay_ext_departure_notice_charge (the customer's surface request). Edges (all state form, all false at frozen_time because the cancelled stay's ledger holds only two collections (installment 1 initial_state.stay_transactions.01eb841f-18d3-48da-a710-b55a6ece6642, 3772.04, and the installment-0 increase initial_state.stay_transactions.9ebf069f-33ad-4f1a-8950-f76899827f2c, 672.00) and no stay_refund_issued row):
 (1) notice charge -> pet-fee refund, state_gate, gate stay_transactions.charge_component, sentence "The notice charge is not collected until the stay's ledger carries the guest-cancellation refund owed on the stay's pet fee." Resolved by refund_pet_fee_41a7068c (agent). Only the pet-fee refund policy books a pet_fee guest_cancellation row.
 (2) notice charge -> extra-guest-fee refund, state_gate, "The notice charge is not collected until the stay's ledger carries the guest-cancellation refund owed on the stay's extra-guest fee." Resolved by refund_extra_guest_fee_b492f389 (agent).
 (3) notice charge -> service-fee refund, state_gate, "The notice charge is not collected until the stay's ledger carries the guest-cancellation refund owed on Roamhaven's guest service fee." Resolved by refund_service_fee_f4bed6e4 (agent).
 (4) service-fee refund -> pet-fee refund, value_input, gate sf_addon_refunds, "The guest-service-fee refund on a cancellation is fixed only after the stay's ledger carries the pet-fee refund that cancellation owes."
 (5) service-fee refund -> extra-guest-fee refund, value_input, gate sf_addon_refunds, "The guest-service-fee refund on a cancellation is fixed only after the stay's ledger carries the extra-guest-fee refund that cancellation owes."
 Four-point test: each sentence joins this policy's own result (the charge's collection / the fee refund's figure) to a record-visible state (a refund entry of a named component on the stay's ledger) with "not ... until" (charge, negated direction: a collection that waits) or "only after" (fee refund, affirmative direction: a figure fixed on what it rests on); no tool, id or code token; strength exact (a hard wait on the entry owed). Derivation: sentence + ledger (no such row) + the depended-on rule ("... part of the pet fee is refunded ... as a pet-fee refund") -> the one write that creates that entry. Topological order: pet, extra-guest (either order, they never read each other), service fee, notice charge. value_input edges = 2 >= max(3-1,1). The tool layer validates nothing: every task tool creates its row unconditionally.
 Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): without the pet-fee refund the service-fee refund evaluates to 26.23, without the extra-guest-fee refund 11.15, without both 6.48 (gold 30.91); skipping any of the three refunds removes its row from the terminal ledger while the charge is still collected.

FACTOR CARD (all figures from the sensitivity run on the handling-time world).
 Notice charge (expected 114.02, all-baseline 6423.55): notice_length (parameter; 75 nights >= 28 -> 30 notice nights; baseline 1 -> 41.39 because the 2 nights kept then fall below the 30-night exemption); later_nights_kept (parameter; a Long-Term stay keeps none of the 44 nights after the notice nights, as its after_check_in_refund_pct is 100; the Moderate tier would keep half and Limited through Super Strict all of them; baseline all kept -> 5131.01); notice_fee_rate (parameter; Long-Term split fee 12.00; baseline 14.20 -> 114.98); notice_tax_exemption (method; 75 and 31 kept nights both meet the 30-night TX-AUSTIN exemption -> 0.00; baseline 17% of the fee base -> 132.52); rewards_fee_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty rewards; Rewards Gold = priority support, no concierge -> 50%; baseline 0 -> 120.55); returning_guest_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty rewards; one credit earning in the last 24 months, 2025-11-17 -> 10%; baseline 0 -> 115.33). Part of the baseline method rather than declared factors (stated in the rule's standard paragraph and varying only by payment plan): the nights the collections paid (one monthly installment = 30 nights; the installment-0 increase is not an installment), the uncollected fees and credit offset (both 0 because installment 1 was collected).
 Pet-fee refund (78.58, all-baseline 0.00): pet_notice_nights (30; baseline 1 -> 130.37); pet_refund_share (monthly with collections begun: 44/75; baseline nightly-refund share 0 -> 0.00); pet_deep_clean_share (cancellation on the check-in date -> 20% kept; baseline 0 -> 87.31); pet_clean_courtesy (rewards; 50% of it waived; baseline -> 69.85); pet_credit_funded_part (rewards ledger: 80.00 redeemed, none reinstated -> card share 0.9921765; baseline -> 79.20; multi-source: credits AND reinstatement evidence).
 Extra-guest-fee refund (331.78, all-baseline 0.00): notice 30 (baseline -> 550.46); share 44/75 (baseline -> 0.00); linen share 10% (baseline -> 349.25); linen courtesy 50% (baseline -> 314.32); credit-funded part (baseline -> 334.40).
 Service-fee refund (30.91, all-baseline 58.27): refund_fee_percentage 12.00 (baseline 14.20 -> 36.57); late_cancellation_fee_share (cancellation dated on or after the check-in date -> 50% of the fee on the refunded base; 75% within 7 days before check-in; all of it earlier; baseline all -> 55.33); arrival_night_courtesy 50% of 108.80 returned in full (multi-source: cancellation date AND Rewards tier; baseline -> 24.43); fee_refund_credit_funded_part (baseline -> 31.15). The refunded fee base is every refunded amount the fee was charged on (nightly, cleaning, pet, extra-guest) for every customer: 0 + 0 + 78.58 + 331.78 = 410.36.
 Near-misses: the 672.00 collection is the installment-0 increase of the accepted guest-count change, not a second monthly installment — counting it would cover 60 nights and wrongly clear the notice charge; the stay was booked at a monthly discount, but the kept night is charged at the booked night price 108.80, not the listing rate 128.00; the guest's 2025 Moderate cancellation (SP3) also carried a service-fee refund but falls outside the 365-day cap window, and the 2026-03-01 refund is the only one inside it (1 < 3); the 2025-11-16 tier_upgrade bonus is not a credit earning; the occupancy tax line on the stay is 0.00 by exemption and the 31 nights kept keep it.

Removing the Rewards membership changes four factors; removing the earning on SP1 changes the returning-guest relief; removing the redemption changes three; removing the installment 1 row changes the nights paid (none) and adds the uncollected fees and the credit offset to the charge; it does not move the pet and extra-guest shares, because the installment-0 collection 9ebf069f still shows that collections have begun on the stay (78.58 and 331.78 again, and the service-fee refund that reads them stays 30.91); removing both collections would drop those shares to their fall-through, the nightly refund on the ledger (0.00). PERSONA. Nadia Petrov, rushed and polite, volunteers only "pay what I owe now"; gives mobile number, then date of birth, then email only on request; the confirmation code and the dog/colleague only when asked; consents passively to Roamhaven's own entries first; runs the payment handed to her with the values the agent gives; closes when told the payment went through. She knows no amounts and never names a refund.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate by phone; verify (phone + DOB); read stays, the stay's requests (the accepted guest-count change), the guest's stay ledger, the Rewards membership and credit ledger, the listing (by the stay's host account) and the host's payout records for the stay; book the pet-fee refund 78.58 and the extra-guest-fee refund 331.78 (either order); book the service-fee refund 30.91 (reads both); unlock and hand over the notice charge; the guest pays 114.02 as installment 2.

VERIFICATION. A temporary script reused check_compute.build_env/eval_compute; the handling-time run gave pet 78.58, extra 331.78, service fee 30.91 (6.48 before the add-on refunds), charge 114.02, and the per-factor figures above. user_scenario:
You are Nadia Petrov, a 40-year-old clinical research coordinator from Austin who travels for hospital contracts and keeps a Roamhaven Rewards membership. You booked a monthly stay at a bungalow in Bouldin Creek, Austin, for a local assignment and checked in this morning with your dog Pepper and a colleague who was sharing the place. At lunchtime your contract was moved to Seattle, so you cancelled the reservation yourself in the Roamhaven app at about 1:40 pm. The app warned you that a monthly stay has a notice period and that you would still owe part of it. You are calling to pay whatever you still owe on this stay, now and from your own card, so it is closed out before your flight tonight. You open with exactly that, a little rushed but polite, and you do not volunteer anything else.
When the agent asks who you are, give your mobile number, 5125551468; if a second detail is needed, give your date of birth, 1986-03-14; only if they still need more, give your email, nadia.petrov@fastmail.com. If asked which reservation, it is the monthly rental at the Bouldin Creek bungalow, confirmation code HMQ7RX42TD, checked in today. You have no idea what the amounts are and never guess one; if the agent asks how much you think you owe, you say you don't know, that is why you are calling. If the agent asks about the dog or your colleague, Pepper and your colleague are both leaving with you today.
You are happy for the agent to take care of anything Roamhaven needs to put through on the reservation before you pay; if they tell you something has to be done first, you say that's fine, go ahead. When the agent hands you the payment to complete yourself, you make it with exactly the reservation, installment number and amount the agent gives you, and you read out the receipt you get. Once the agent tells you the payment has gone through and the reservation is settled, you thank them and say goodbye; you have nothing else to raise.
